the rectenna is able to harvest RF energy from the ambient Wi-Fi band and convert it into DC power, with a conversion efficiency higher than 40 % for an input power density in the order of −10 dBm.

we have demonstrated the first rectenna operating at 2.4 GHz in paper substrate, with a compact design, a high efficiency and a low power consumption, which can be a key element in the realization of a wireless sensor network powered by RF energy harvesting.

paper is a viable substrate for low power rectennas, and that the proposed prototype could be useful for powering wireless sensors in the Wi-Fi frequency band.

the proposed rectenna can be used in low-power wireless sensor network applications and in the development of low-cost, ultra-lightweight and low-power wireless sensors for environmental monitoring, health-care and smart-cities.
